title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
abstract: arXiv:2611.28489v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. Does this carry over to \emph{open} generators, and if not, what fails? We answer with \textbf{Open Vision Banana (OVB)}, an open framework that adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance, and referring segmentation, using a single shared low-rank adapter and public data. Each task is a \emph{task contract} whose RGB encoder, instruction, and decoder share one specification and are checked before training. Studying 42 externally evaluated checkpoints from two 100k-update runs, six exact weight-space merges, and eight controlled shorter runs, we find that the gap to the closed system is specific and measurable. Geometry is learned early while absolute scale is not: median-aligned NYUv2 $\delta_1$ stays at 0.89--0

translated_title: Open Vision Banana：一个通过RGB空间生成实现统一视觉感知的开放框架
translated_abstract: Vision Banana 表明，一个经过指令微调、将感知输出绘制为RGB图像的闭源图像生成器，可以成为一个通用视觉模型。那么这是否适用于开放生成器？如果不适用，问题出在哪里？我们用 **Open Vision Banana (OVB)** 来回答这个问题——一个开放框架，它将 Qwen-Image-2.1 的 7B 扩散生成器改造为一个指令驱动的模型，可完成度量深度估计、语义分割、实例分割和指代分割，仅使用一个共享的低秩适配器和公开数据。每个任务都是一个“任务契约”，其RGB编码器、指令和解码器共享同一规范，并在训练前进行检查。通过研究来自两次10万步更新运行的42个外部评估检查点、六次精确的权重空间合并以及八次受控的较短运行，我们发现与闭源系统的差距是特定且可测量的：几何结构能被早期习得，而绝对尺度则不能——中位数对齐的 NYUv2 δ₁ 保持在 0.89–0.9（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出开放框架 Open Vision Banana (OVB)，仅用单一共享低秩适配器和公开数据，通过“任务契约”机制将 Qwen-Image-2.1 的 7B 扩散生成器改造为指令驱动的统一视觉感知模型，并发现其与闭源系统的差距是特定且可测量的——几何能早期习得而绝对尺度难以掌握。
en_tdlr: Open Vision Banana (OVB) is an open framework that adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into a single instruction-driven unified visual perception model using one shared low-rank adapter and task contracts, showing that the gap to closed systems is specific and measurable—geometry is learned early while absolute scale is not.
